The '''GAZ-66''' is a [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] and Russian [[four wheel drive|4x4]] all-road (off-road) military truck produced by [[GAZ]]. It was one of<!--The US Field Manual FM-100-2-3 dated 6 June 1991 says that a Motorized Rifle Division's truck fleet included 421 Ural-375 Trucks and 344 GAZ-66.--> the main cargo <!--'transport' - this can mislead people into thinking that the trucks carried infantry, when they were actually used for ammo, equipment etc. The infantry were in BTR-60/70/80 wheeled APCs or BMP-1/2/3 tracked IFVs.--> vehicles for [[motorized infantry]] of the [[Soviet Army]] and is still employed in former [[Soviet Union]] countries.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.military-today.com/trucks/gaz_66.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070705063700if_/http://www.military-today.com/trucks/gaz_66.htm|url-status=usurped|archive-date=July 5, 2007|title=GAZ-66 - Light utility truck|access-date=2019-04-24}}</ref> It is nicknamed ''[[shishiga]]'' (шишига), ''shisharik'' (шишарик)/''shehsherik'' (шешерик), ''trueman'' (in [[Siberia]]).

== History ==
After tests and trials, in 1969 GAZ-66 received the [[state quality mark of the USSR]]. It was the first USSR truck to receive such an award.<ref>Л. Д. Гоголев. Автомобили в боевом строю. М., "Молодая гвардия", 1981.</ref>

Almost one million vehicles of this type were built for both military and civilian use. The GAZ-66 has gained legendary status in many countries due to its reliability, simplicity and off-road capability.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://englishrussia.com/2016/11/08/maybe-the-best-soviet-truck-legend-of-soviet-union-gaz-66/|title=Maybe the best Soviet truck, Legend of Soviet Union – GAZ-66 {{!}} English Russia|date=8 November 2016 |access-date=2019-04-24}}</ref> Since the 1960s, the GAZ-66 has been popular with armed forces and off-road enthusiasts.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://auto-market-usa.com/auto-classified-ads/russian-4wd-truck-gaz-66-for-hunters-and-off-road-travelers/|title=Russian 4wd truck GAZ-66 for hunters and off-road travelers | work = Auto Market USA: Auto Classifieds |language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-24|archive-date=2019-04-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190424143204/https://auto-market-usa.com/auto-classified-ads/russian-4wd-truck-gaz-66-for-hunters-and-off-road-travelers/|url-status=usurped}}</ref> Production ceased in 1999, with the [[GAZ-3308]] being produced instead.

==Basic versions==
[[File:Tolna Feuerwehr 0032.JPG|thumb|GAZ-66 based fire engine]]
[[File:A_GAZ-66_truck_at_Tambov_Airshow_2007.jpg|thumb|right|GAZ-66 tanker]]
[[File:GAZ_66.jpg|thumb|GAZ-66 with [[KUNG]] body.]]
[[File:ГАЗ-66_в_Хабаровске.JPG|thumb|right|GAZ-66 platform truck]]
[[File:GAZ-66_truck_in_Russian_military_service%2C_used_as_a_communication_centre.jpg|thumb|right|GAZ-66 in Russian military service]]
[[File:ASC Leiden - Coutinho Collection - G 20 - Life in Ziguinchor, Senegal - PAIGC office in Ziguinchor, also Coutinho’s home - 1973.tif|GAZ-66 in military service with the [[PAIGC]] liberation movement in [[Guinea-Bissau]], 1973|thumb]]

* GAZ-66-1 (1964–1968) – the first model with no centralized system for adjusting the air pressure in the tires
* GAZ-66A (1964–1968) – with a winch
* GAZ-34 – a 6×6 prototype
* GAZ-66B (1966) – Paratrooper version with telescopic steering column, folding roof and folding windshield frame
** BM-21V "Grad-V" (Vozdushnodesantiy – 'airborne') (NATO designation M1975): Developed for airborne troops in 1969. A GAZ-66B 4x4 truck chassis is fitted with a 12-round 122&nbsp;mm rocket launcher. The vehicle is sturdy enough to be air-dropped. Parts of the vehicle such as the canvas cab roof can be taken off or folded down to reduce its size during transit. Like the [[BM-21]], the BM-21V has stabilizing jacks on the rear of the vehicle for support when firing. The launch vehicle has the industrial index of 9P125.
* GAZ-66D (1964–1968) – the chassis with a power take-off
* GAZ-66P – tractor (experimental)
* GAZ-66E (1964–1968) – with shielded electrical equipment
* GAZ-66-01 (1968–1985) – the base model with a centralized control system for tire pressure
* GAZ-66-02 (1968–1985) – with a winch
* GAZ-66-03 (1964–1968) – with shielded electrical equipment
* GAZ-66-04 (1968–1985) – the chassis with shielded electrical equipment
* GAZ-66-05 (1968–1985) – with shielded electrical equipment and a winch
* GAZ-66-11 (1985–1996) – upgraded base model
* GAZ-66-12 (1985–1996) – with a winch
* GAZ-66-14 (1985–1996) – the chassis with shielded electrical equipment and a power take-off

==Military versions==
* GAZ-66-15 (1985–1996) – with shielded electrical equipment and a winch
* GAZ-66-16 (1991–1993) – modernized version with ZMZ-513.10, reinforced tires (wheels – lean), completed the brakes, the platform without intruding wheel niches (also installed on GAZ-66-11 and GAZ-66-40 ), load capacity 2.3 tons
* GAZ-66-21 (1993–1995) – the national-economic modification with the dual tires and rear axle wooden platform GAZ-53, load capacity 3.5 tons
* GAZ-66-31 – chassis for trucks
* GAZ-66-41 (1992–1995) – a naturally aspirated GAZ-544 diesel engine
* GAZ-66-40 (1995–1999) – with a GAZ-5441 turbodiesel
* GAZ-66-92 (1987–1995) – for use in the far north
* GAZ-66-96 – chassis for [[shift bus]]es

===Export versions===
* GAZ-66-51 (1968–1985)
* GAZ-66-52 (1968–1985) – with a winch
* GAZ-66-81 (1985–1995) – for countries with a temperate climate
* GAZ-66-91 (1985–1995) – for countries with a tropical climate

===Specialised versions===
* AP-2 – aid station, the main transport unit regimental aid station.
* AS-66 – ambulance, designed to evacuate the wounded.
* DDA-2 – disinfecting shower installation, is used in the military (sometimes civil) sanitary-epidemiological units.
* GZSA-731, 983A, 947, 3713, 3714 – Vans "Mail", "bread" and "Medicine"
* MZ-66 – Lube.
* 3902, 3903, 39021, 39031 – mobile workshops to provide technical assistance to agricultural machinery.
* 2001, 2002, 3718, 3719, 3716, 3924, 39521 – mobile clinics
* NZAS-3964, Volgar-39461 – [[watch bus]]es
* GAZ-SAZ-3511 – tipper for agricultural purposes on the GAZ-66-31 (build – Saransk).
* GAZ-KAZ-3511 – tipper for agricultural purposes on GAZ-66-31 (build – Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan)

== Specifications ==
Specifications for GAZ-66-11<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://weaponsystems.net/weaponsystem/CC08%20-%20GAZ-66.html|title=GAZ-66 {{!}} Weaponsystems.net|website=weaponsystems.net|access-date=2019-04-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Основные ТТХ серийного ГАЗ-66-11 (1985–1996)|url=http://www.voengruzovik.ru/GAZ/GAZ-66/GAZ-66-11.htm|access-date=2014-03-02|archive-date=2016-03-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304084547/http://www.voengruzovik.ru/GAZ/GAZ-66/GAZ-66-11.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>
;Design
* Cab-forward design, 2-seat cab + 21 passengers in the back.
* Payload: {{convert|2000|kg|abbr=on}} plus the same weight trailer
* Suspension: Solid axles with leaf springs
;Engine
* Type- ZMZ-66-06 V8 petrol (carburetor) OHV engine; heavy duty version of the [[GAZ-53|ZMZ-53]]<ref>[https://tractorreview.ru/dvigateli/zmz/zmz-511-tehnicheskie-harakteristiki.html ЗМЗ-511: технические характеристики]</ref><ref>[https://avtomobilgaz.ru/gruzovye/gaz3307/dvigatel.html Двигатели на ГАЗ 3307]</ref><ref>[https://gaz24.info/wp/dvygately-v8-zmz-konstrukcyja-harakterystyky-ystoryja-razrabotky/ Двигатели V8 ЗМЗ конструкция, характеристики, история разработки]</ref>
* Displacement: 4,254 cc (Bore {{convert|92|mm|in|3|abbr=on}}, Stroke {{convert|80|mm|in|3|abbr=on}})
* Compression ratio: 7.6:1
* Output: {{convert|120|hp|abbr=on}} @ 3,200 rpm
* Torque: {{convert|284.5|N.m|0|abbr=on}} @ 2,000-2200 rpm
* Max. speed- {{convert|90|km/h|abbr=on}}(speed governed)
;Brakes
* Type: Drums, with hydraulic control, single circuit, servo assisted
* Stopping distance from 20&nbsp;mph: 27'
;Measurements
* L×W×H: {{convert|5805|mm|ftin|0|abbr=on}} x {{convert|2322|mm|ftin|0|abbr=on}} x {{convert|2490|mm|ftin|0|abbr=on}}(cab) / {{convert|2520|mm|ftin|0|abbr=on}}(tent)
* Wheelbase: {{convert|3300|mm|in|2|abbr=on}}
* Track front/rear: {{convert|1820|mm|in|2|abbr=on}}/{{convert|1750|mm|in|2|abbr=on}}
* Curb weight: {{convert|3440|kg|abbr=on}}
* Fuel tanks: 2 x {{convert|105|L|abbr=on}}
* Fuel economy: {{convert|31.5|L/100km|0|abbr=on}}
;Maneuverability
* Turning circle: {{convert|9.5|m|ft|0|abbr=on}}
* Approach angle: 41°
* Departure angle: 32°
* Max. ascent angle: 31–37° (fully loaded)
* Ground clearance: {{convert|315|mm|in|0|abbr=on}}
* Fording depth: {{convert|1|m|in|0|abbr=on}}
;Tires
* Size: 12–18"
* Pressure: Adjustable with central tyre inflation system from cab

==Popular culture==
[[File:The Soviet Union 1971 CPA 3998 stamp (GAZ-66 Truck).jpg|thumb|Soviet stamp, 1971]]
* In the 2010 game ''[[Call of Duty: Black Ops]]'', the GAZ-66 is used as a transport for guards in the level "Vorkuta".
* It is mentioned in the 1991 [[Tom Clancy]] novel ''[[The Sum Of All Fears]]''. 
* In the Russian version of the TV show ''[[Top Gear Russia|Top Gear]]'', a test was conducted on the vehicle's strengths: the body had building rubble dropped on it, it was set on fire and submerged in water. After all these tests, it kept going.
* The GAZ-66 was featured in the movie ''[[The Expendables 2]]'' with [[Jean-Claude Van Damme]].
* The GAZ-66 is a truck in the game ''[[Spintires: MudRunner|MudRunner]]'' with the name of B-66 due to copyright claims.
* In the 2019 [[HBO]] TV miniseries ''[[Chernobyl (miniseries)|Chernobyl]]'', the truck is used by Gen. Col. Vladimir Pikalov, commander of the Soviet Chemical Troops, to carry out a radiation measuring at the damaged power plant, with high-range [[dosimeter]] placed at the front and lead sheets covering the cabin.
* In the 2020 film Wonder Woman 1984. Appears in the Middle Eastern convoy scene.
